checks.name: message_cache_injection_coherence

evidence.reason: Deep copy, stream buffering, response-channel swap, and pending-entry creation.
Fresh deep snapshots in acceptance order.
Delivers private copy into normal ingress; removes only on confirmed acceptance; classified errors preserve the entry.
Sole consumer of the wrapped transport channel; no bypass while capture is enabled.

checks.reason: CapturingTransport.serve is the sole consumer of the wrapped transport's Consumer channel; capture deep-copies the command, buffers one-shot snapshot streams, and swaps rpc.RespChan so requests are retained before delivery. Pending() returns fresh deep copies, Inject delivers the controller-private copy through the normal target ingress, and Drop/Clear/Inject invalidate handles and preserve entries on every classified failure. Request and response are cached as separate entries with reversed routing and new handles.

checks.name: original_send_suppressed

evidence.reason: Controlled path invokes capture and does not forward the original RPC.
Delivers the controller-owned RPC copy, not the original.

checks.reason: While capture is enabled, handleRPC calls capture and never forwards the original RPC; capture builds a controller-owned copy and swaps the response channel. Only Inject delivers a message into the target's consumer channel, so the original exchange is suppressed until explicit injection.

checks.name: protocol_logic_unchanged

evidence.reason: Falls back to time.After when no controller is installed.
Falls back to randomExtra when no RandomController is installed.
Returns immediately when the node is not paused.

checks.reason: With nil Config.TimeController and Config.RandomController (the production defaults), r.timeAfter/r.timeNow delegate to time.After/time.Now, randomTimeout uses the original rand.Int63()%minVal staggering, InmemTransport.after delegates to time.After, and the pause gate is a no-op when not paused. No protocol transition, persistence, ordering, or message semantics change.

checks.name: testing_contract_conformance

evidence.reason: Sets the paused flag and returns without waiting for execution contexts to reach the gate.
Gate is only checked at the top of each loop iteration, leaving the select below it able to process an event after Pause returns.
Gate at 166 precedes the select at 171, so a select already entered can process an RPC after Pause.

checks.reason: The lifecycle Pause operation does not reach its promised boundary before returning. Pause only sets a flag and returns; a state loop or replication/FSM/snapshot goroutine that has already passed its pause gate (or is currently blocked in its select) can still handle one more protocol message, consume a timer, and emit output after Pause returns, weakening the fixed pause_resume guarantee that Pause prevents message handling, subject time progress, and protocol output.

issues.reason: Pause returns before all required execution contexts reach the paused boundary. It sets paused=true and returns immediately; the state loops (runFollower/runCandidate/leaderLoop), replicate/heartbeat/pipelineReplicate/pipelineDecode, runFSM, and runSnapshots only check lifecyclePauseGate at the top of their next iteration. A goroutine that has already passed the gate or is blocked in its select can handle one in-flight (or newly arriving) protocol message, consume a timer, and produce output after Pause returns. This is a reachable, concurrency-related weakening of the fixed guarantee that Pause prevents message handling, time progress, and protocol output, and is therefore a blocking issue rather than a disclosed residual risk.

risks: Stop and Crash converge to the same Shutdown path in this target because Raft persists term/vote/log eagerly and Shutdown performs no shutdown-time flush; the controller records phase=stopped vs phase=crashed so Restart preserves the required stop/crash distinction, but Crash does perform target-defined transport cleanup (WithClose) rather than a purely abrupt discard.

PendingMessage.Message is the minimal existing WithRPCHeader common interface rather than a richer typed variant carrier; consumers must type-assert to concrete command types (guided by MessageKind) to access message payloads.

A copy or stream-buffer failure in MessageController.capture is surfaced only by completing the original sender's exchange with an error (handleRPC discards the returned error), so the failure is observable to the remote sender but not through a dedicated controller error/state.

Inject to a paused target succeeds (its buffered consumer channel accepts) and removes the entry rather than returning ErrTargetUnavailable; the message is queued and processed only after Resume, which is a cross-capability ambiguity but does not lose the message.

Advance(n) loops n units without yielding to node goroutines; a timer re-armed in reaction to a delivered step is exposed to a later boundary exactly like back-to-back Advance(1) calls, but the interleaving of node processing between steps is scheduler-dependent and not synchronized by the controller.
